Simulate data from the ZISAR model

Source: R/simulate.R
rzisar.Rd

Draws one data set from the ZISAR model, on a regular lattice with queen contiguity (the Monte Carlo design of the ZISAR paper) or on a weights matrix supplied by the user. Covariates are independent standard normal; the first element of beta and of gamma is the intercept. zero_spatial adds spatial structure to the inflation predictor: a SAR field with one element per unit ("field", the general model of the paper) or a SAR filter on \(Z\gamma\) ("sar"); see zisar().

Usage

rzisar(
  n_side,
  beta,
  rho,
  gamma,
  kappa = 2,
  sigma = 0.5,
  zero_spatial = c("none", "field", "sar"),
  rho0 = 0,
  sigma0 = 0,
  W = NULL
)

Arguments

n_side

Side of the square lattice, so \(n\) = n_side^2 units. Ignored when W is supplied.

beta

Count-process coefficients, intercept first.

rho

Spatial autoregressive parameter, in \((-1, 1)\).

gamma

Zero-inflation coefficients, intercept first.

kappa

Negative binomial shape.

sigma

Standard deviation of the random effects.

zero_spatial

Inflation predictor: "none" (restricted model), "field" or "sar".

rho0, sigma0

Spatial autoregressive parameter and standard deviation of the inflation field ("field"), or parameter of the filter ("sar", which takes no sigma0).

W

Optional row-standardised weights matrix (or spdep listw) to use instead of the lattice.

Value

A list with

data

Data frame with the counts y, the count covariates x1, x2, ... and the inflation covariates z1, z2, ..., ready for zisar(y ~ x1 + ... | z1 + ..., data = data, W = W).

W

The weights matrix (sparse).

coords

Lattice coordinates (row, col), for example for zisar_basis(); NULL with a user-supplied W.

truth

The parameters used.

eta, g, zeta, mu, pi, s

Latent field, inflation field (zero without one), inflation predictor, negative binomial means, inflation probabilities and structural-zero indicators.

Examples

set.seed(42)
sim <- rzisar(15, beta = c(1, 0.5, -0.3), rho = 0.5, gamma = c(-1, 0.7))
head(sim$data)
#>   y         x1         x2         z1
#> 1 6  1.3709584 -0.1740182 -1.3038212
#> 2 0 -0.5646982  0.5156677 -0.2509145
#> 3 0  0.3631284 -0.2343653  0.1710074
#> 4 0  0.6328626 -0.6585034 -0.4034675
#> 5 7  0.4042683  1.2502366  0.1046594
#> 6 4 -0.1061245 -0.2717637 -0.3188808
mean(sim$data$y == 0)
#> [1] 0.4622222

# Structural zeros clustered by a field of their own
sim2 <- rzisar(15, beta = c(1, 0.5), rho = 0.5, gamma = c(-1, 0.7),
               zero_spatial = "field", rho0 = 0.8, sigma0 = 1)
cor(sim2$g, as.numeric(sim2$W %*% sim2$g))
#> [1] 0.7777463
